statement: Good Boy is a 2025 American supernatural horror film directed by Ben Leonberg.
The film stars Leonberg's own Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever dog, Indy, in the leading role as himself.
Shane Jensen, Arielle Friedman, and Larry Fessenden are in supporting roles in Good Boy.
Good Boy is primarily set in a rural woodland house.
Good Boy follows Indy and his owner, Todd (Jensen), a young man with a chronic lung disease, as they move into Todd's late grandfather's rural home.
A malevolent supernatural presence gradually engulfs Todd in Good Boy.
Indy, Todd's devoted dog, attempts to rescue him in the film Good Boy.
Good Boy is Ben Leonberg's feature directorial debut.
Ben Leonberg conceived the idea for Good Boy after re-watching Poltergeist (1982).
Leonberg noted that dogs in haunted house films often sense the presence of ghosts before humans do.
Leonberg decided to write a traditional haunted house film from the perspective of a dog.
Leonberg co-wrote the screenplay for Good Boy with Alex Cannon beginning in 2017.
The screenplay for Good Boy emphasized action and perspective over dialogue to reflect the dog's point of view.
Indy had no prior acting experience before being cast in Good Boy.
Leonberg cast Indy as the lead in Good Boy.
Principal photography for Good Boy took place in Harding Township, New Jersey.
Principal photography for Good Boy took place over three years.
Good Boy was filmed on a $70,000 budget.
For much of the filming process of Good Boy, only Indy, Leonberg, and producer Kari Fischer were on set.
Kari Fischer is Leonberg's wife.
Good Boy premiered at the 2025 South by Southwest Film & TV Festival on March 8, 2025.
Good Boy was released theatrically in the United States on October 3, 2025.
Independent Film Company (IFC) and Shudder released Good Boy theatrically in the United States.
To date, Good Boy has grossed $8.5 million worldwide.
Critical reviews for Good Boy were generally positive.
Reviewers commended Good Boy's ambitious concept, technical craftsmanship, visual style, and emotionally resonant themes.
Reviewers commended Indy's performance in the lead role in Good Boy.
Some critics were critical of Good Boy's storytelling.
Critics cited a convoluted narrative and pacing issues in Good Boy.
Todd, a young man suffering from a chronic lung disease, relocates from New York City to his late grandfather's rural, uninhabited home in the woods.
Todd's dog is a Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever named Indy.
Todd's sister, Vera, worries about Todd's isolation at the home.
Vera believes the house is haunted and contributed to their grandfather's death there.
Indy immediately senses a presence in the home.
The presence in the home often manifests in shadows and sometimes appears as a dark, skeletal figure drenched in mud.
While roaming the woods, Indy and Todd encounter Richard, a longtime neighbor.
Richard warns Indy and Todd of fox traps he has set in the area.
Richard informs Todd that he was the one who found Todd's grandfather's corpse.
Todd's grandfather's Golden Retriever, Bandit, has been missing since his death.
Indy recurrently observes the dark entity in the house.
Indy encounters an apparition of Bandit which leads him upstairs.
Beneath a wardrobe, Indy finds a bandana that belonged to Bandit.
Indy experiences recurring dreams of being attacked by the dark figure.
Indy has visions of Todd's grandfather.
Todd's grandfather appears to have died in the home of a similar disease to Todd's.
Todd's health worsens and he begins regularly coughing up blood.
Todd becomes increasingly aggressive toward Indy and Vera.
Vera constantly checks in on Todd by phone.
Late one night, Indy awakens to find Todd in an incoherent state, slamming his head against the basement door.
While Todd sleeps, Indy observes the figure approaching the bedroom.
Todd awakens and collapses.
Todd is separated from Indy after the entity closes a door between them.
Indy escapes the house, intending to find Richard so he can help Todd.
Indy becomes caught in one of Richard's fox snares.
Todd reprimands Indy by leashing him outside and forcing him to sleep in a doghouse.
While outside one night, Indy senses the dark figure.
Indy hears Todd coughing loudly from the upstairs bedroom.
The figure attempts to attack Indy.
Indy breaks free by running into the doghouse, knocking it over and breaking the chain from its anchor inside.
Indy finds the home's cellar door open and infiltrates the home.
Indy encounters Bandit's skeleton in the process of infiltrating the home.
The dark figure approaches Todd in his bedroom while he is in a weakened, rapidly deteriorating state.
Indy arrives in the bedroom and comforts Todd.
Todd turns and faces his own corpse on the bed.
Todd realizes he has died.
Todd is dragged by the figure through the house and into the basement.
Indy chases Todd, attempting to save him as he is pulled into a dark, cavernous tunnel.
Todd accepts his fate.
Todd tells Indy he is a good dog but cannot rescue him.
The dark figure seizes Todd.
The following morning, Vera arrives at the house.
Vera finds Todd's dead body and Indy sitting alone at the bottom of the cellar entrance.
Vera tearfully calls for Indy.
Indy pauses after hearing Todd's whistling from the tunnel.
Indy ascends the stairs to Vera.
Indy plays himself, a Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever, in the film.
Shane Jensen plays Todd, Indy's owner.
Arielle Friedman plays Vera, Todd's sister.
Larry Fessenden plays Todd's grandfather.
Stuart Rudin plays Richard, Todd's neighbor.
Max plays Bandit, the Golden Retriever owned by Todd and Vera's grandfather.
In 2012, Ben Leonberg conceived the idea for a supernatural horror film framed from a dog's perspective.
Leonberg re-watched the 1982 film Poltergeist.
In Poltergeist, the central family's dog is the first to sense the presence of ghosts.
Leonberg realized that dogs sensing ghosts first was a trope among other horror films centered around a haunted house.
Leonberg cited the 1980 film The Shining as an influence for Good Boy.
Both The Shining and Good Boy question whether the characters' seemingly supernatural experiences are genuine or products of their psychological state.
Both The Shining and Good Boy feature endings open to interpretation.
Leonberg and his co-writer Alex Cannon began writing the film in 2017.
Leonberg envisioned Good Boy as a tribute to dogs and their relationship with humans.
Cannon and Leonberg wrote the story to emphasize action, perspective, and point of view because the story could not utilize dialogue to progress.
The film Good Boy was directed by Leonberg in his feature directorial debut.
Good Boy was produced by Kari Fischer, Leonberg's wife.
They cast their dog, Indy, a Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever, as the film's lead.
The decision to cast Indy came after Leonberg participated in The Rode Reel, an online short film competition, with an entry starring Indy.
The short film starring Indy won the Judges' Film Prize.
The short film starring Indy won a financial award that helped fund the full-length feature Good Boy.
Indy earned a nomination for Best Actor for his performance in the short film.
Encouraged by the film's reception and Indy's recognition, Leonberg chose to cast him as the lead in Good Boy.
Indy had no formal acting training prior to Good Boy.
Leonberg originally did not picture Indy as the lead while writing Good Boy.
Leonberg described Indy as having an 'intense, unblinking stare' and expressive movements.
Leonberg thought Indy's characteristics would make him a good fit for the role.
To begin production, Leonberg developed a loose storyboard.
Leonberg recognized that it was impossible to plan each shot with complete precision, as Indy's movements were unpredictable and could not be timed like those of a human actor.
Cinematography and lighting for Good Boy were adapted to account for the dog's unpredictable movement.
Good Boy was filmed over a period of three years in a house in Harding Township, New Jersey.
The filming of Good Boy accounted for over 400 days of filming.
The lengthy filming schedule was accredited to Indy not having a double.
Indy portrayed himself in every scene of the film Good Boy.
Leonberg, Fischer, and Indy lived in the house during Good Boy's production.
For much of the principal photography, only Fischer, Leonberg, and Indy were present on set to keep the filming process free of distractions.
Leonberg said that they frequently completed only one or two shots per day due to the difficulty of working with a dog.
To direct Indy, Leonberg would make bizarre noises and say unusual words in strange vocal tones to elicit a natural reaction from the animal.
To make Indy walk in certain directions, a toy dog was used to guide him.
Leonberg stated that much of Indy's performance was crafted through filming and post-production techniques, such as music, sound design, and the Kuleshov effect.
The Kuleshov effect was used to convey audience interpretation rather than emotional expression from the animal.
The film Good Boy aimed to capture a dog's point of view.
Leonberg and the film's cinematographer, Wade Grebnoel, utilized visual techniques such as filming from a low angle to frame Indy in the center to prioritize his viewpoint.
Leonberg and Grebnoel rarely showed human characters above the waist in Good Boy.
Leonberg would occasionally stand in for Shane Jensen as Todd in shots where the character's face is off-screen.
Indy would only perform certain actions with his real-life owner.
A stuffed replica of Indy, which Leonberg nicknamed 'Findy', was used as a stand-in for Indy when setting up various shots of the film.
The stuffed replica 'Findy' was used for performing stunts.
Good Boy uses limited computer-generated imagery.
None of the computer-generated imagery in Good Boy was used to enhance Indy's performance.
Leonberg and Fischer set up their own production company for the film, called What's Wrong With Your Dog?
The film Good Boy was completed on a production budget of $70,000.
Good Boy has a 73-minute runtime.
Good Boy premiered at the 2025 South by Southwest Film & TV Festival on March 8 in the Alamo Drafthouse Cinema in Austin, Texas.
Good Boy screened again at the Overlook Film Festival in New Orleans in April 2025.
The film had its Canadian premiere at the Calgary Underground Film Festival.
Good Boy was screened in July 2025 at the Fantasia International Film Festival in Montreal, Quebec.
The film was originally scheduled for a limited theatrical release.
The popularity of Good Boy's trailer and poster achieved the largest reach in the Independent Film Company's (IFC) history.
The popularity of Good Boy's trailer and poster led to it receiving a wide theatrical release.
In May 2025, the streaming service Shudder acquired the distribution rights to Good Boy for Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, and the United States.
Good Boy was screened at the Melbourne International Film Festival on August 8.
Good Boy was screened at the Film at Lincoln Center on August 19, 2025.
Good Boy was released theatrically throughout North America on October 3, 2025 via the IFC.
In the United Kingdom and Ireland, Good Boy was released in theaters on October 10, via Vertigo Releasing.
Good Boy was released on streaming on October 24.
Good Boy premiered on Shudder on November 21.
Good Boy grossed $990,000 on its domestic opening night.
On its opening Saturday, Good Boy grossed $777,700.
Throughout its opening weekend, Good Boy was screened at 1,650 theaters.
Good Boy's opening weekend theater count was IFC's second-highest in its history.
Good Boy grossed $2.3 million throughout its opening weekend.
Good Boy debuted as the ninth-highest-grossing film of its opening weekend.
Good Boy's opening weekend gross was IFC's second-best in history.
Within the larger IFC Entertainment Group, Good Boy ranked as the third-largest opening weekend.
Good Boy's opening weekend ranking was behind Clown in a Cornfield (2025) and Late Night with the Devil (2023).
Clown in a Cornfield (2025) was released by RLJ Entertainment.
In its second weekend, Good Boy stayed in 1,650 theaters.
Good Boy earned about $1.36 million over its second weekend.
Good Boy earned $1.6 million over the long four-day period of its second weekend.
By its third weekend, Good Boy had earned $5.59 million domestically.
By its third weekend, Good Boy had earned over $450,000 internationally.
To date, Good Boy has grossed $8.7 million at the worldwide box office.
Good Boy received generally positive reviews.
Critics commended Good Boy's craftsmanship and technical execution given the challenges of its concept.
Chase Hutchison of TheWrap said the film 'thrives in its technical approach'.
Benjamin Lee of The Guardian called Good Boy a strong showcase of Leonberg's capabilities, despite having limited resources.
Critics responded positively to Good Boy's cinematography and visuals.
Fangoria critic Jordan Hoffman described Good Boy as a 'marvel of imagery' for its vivid outdoor visuals and the haunting atmosphere of its indoor scenes.
Wendy Ide of The Observer described the film as 'cleverly framed and murkily atmospheric'.
Reviewers lauded Indy's performance as the lead in Good Boy.
Mick LaSalle of the San Francisco Chronicle described Indy's performance as 'a marvel of sensitivity, alertness and nuance'.
Rendy Jones of Den of Geek likened Indy's performance to the title character of the animated comedy horror series Courage the Cowardly Dog.
Carlos Morales of IGN cited Indy's performance as the primary reason to watch the film.
Many critics appreciated the novelty of Good Boy's premise.
Good Boy's storytelling received a mixed response.
Some critics considered Good Boy's storytelling to be convoluted, underwhelming, and thinly scripted.
In the Los Angeles Times, critic Amy Nicholson called the film's story underwhelming and restrained.
Kevin Maher of The Times was critical of the story's plot holes and pacing inconsistencies in Good Boy.
Some critics also criticized Good Boy for feeling drawn out, despite its relatively short runtime.
Many voiced that they found the film emotionally moving and thought-provoking.
Peter Debruge (Variety) and Meagan Navarro (Bloody Disgusting) both agreed that Good Boy's emotional impact stemmed from Indy's immense loyalty to his owner.
Debruge and Navarro found that Indy's loyalty deepened their appreciation for dogs.
Most critics found the film to be effectively scary and suspenseful.
The Hollywood Reporter's Frank Scheck and IndieWire's Rafael Motamayor both noted that Good Boy's scares felt familiar and unoriginal.
Scheck and Motamayor noted that Good Boy's scares remained effective throughout the runtime.
Kim Newman, writing for the British Film Institute, called the film 'a study in creeping dread rather than shocks'.
On the review aggregator website Rotten Tomatoes, Good Boy holds an approval rating of 91% based on 179 reviews.

Rotten Tomatoes' consensus states: 'Good Boy is a visually striking, emotionally devastating horror film that eschews genre conventions to deliver a uniquely haunting and conceptually ambitious experience.'
On Metacritic, Good Boy has a weighted average score of 73 out of 100 based on reviews from 21 critics.
The Metacritic score indicates 'generally favorable' reviews for Good Boy.
Both Ian Sandwell of Digital Spy and Rafael Motamayor of IndieWire called Good Boy one of the year's best horror movies.
The National Board of Review, at its 2025 ceremony, listed Good Boy as one of the year's ten best independent films.
Audiences polled by CinemaScore gave Good Boy an average grade of 'B' on an A+ to F scale.
In 2025, Indy received the Howl of Fame Award – Best Canine Performance at the 2025 South by Southwest Film & TV Festival.
In 2025, Good Boy received the Scariest Feature Film award at the Overlook Film Festival.
In 2025, Good Boy received the Great Filmmaking Award from People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals.
In 2025, Good Boy received the Best Motion Picture Award at the 58th Sitges Film Festival.
In 2025, Good Boy received the Best International Feature Film award at the Strasbourg European Fantastic Film Festival.
In 2025, Good Boy received the Fresh Blood Award at Fantasy Filmfest.
In 2026, Good Boy received the Best First Feature award at the 9th Astra Film Awards.
In 2026, Indy received the Best Performance in a Horror or Thriller award at the 9th Astra Film Awards.
